title: LAION-BVD: 10 Million Hours of Open Video
hook: 1.3 billion video URLs mined from CommonCrawl, 80 million downloaded, synthetically captioned for video, audio, and image pretraining — and released openly.
key_points: 1.3B platform-specific video URLs collected from CommonCrawl; 80M videos actually downloaded, totalling 10 million hours.
Built for multimodal pretraining across video, audio, and image modalities at once.
Content-aware scene detection splits videos into clips, which get synthetically generated video and audio captions.
Models trained on it are competitive on video-text and audio-text benchmarks, improving consistently with training and model scale.
Scene-changing frames form an image-text corpus with a visual distribution unlike standard web images, and train strong image-text retrieval.
content_html: Open multimodal research has long had a data problem on the video side: image-text pairs are abundant and public, but the video corpora behind frontier models are not. Hochlehnert, Nezhurina, and colleagues at LAION address that with LAION-BVD, assembled by mining CommonCrawl for 1.3 billion platform-specific video URLs, then downloading 80 million videos — 10 million hours in total.
extra_html:
How it is built

Content-aware scene detection splits the videos into clips, and both video and audio captions are generated synthetically for each. That gives a corpus usable for video, audio, and image pretraining from a single pipeline. The authors report models trained on it performing competitively on standard video-text and audio-text benchmarks, with gains that keep coming as training or model scale increases — the property you want from a pretraining corpus.

An unexpected byproduct

They also test video frames as a substitute for web image-text data, extracting scene-changing frames. Those frames sit in a visibly different distribution from the usual scraped-image corpora, yet models trained on them reach strong image-text retrieval — suggesting video is a viable and largely untapped source of image supervision. The dataset is released to the community.

related.title: LAION-5B: Open Image-Text at Scale
related.hook: CLIP and DALL-E showed huge, noisy image-text data is gold. LAION-5B made that public — billions of CLIP-filtered pairs anyone can train open models on.

related.title: The Pile: 800GB of Diverse Text
related.hook: Web text alone leaves gaps. The Pile stitches together 22 curated sources — academic and professional — so a language model picks up knowledge plain web crawls miss.

related.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes LMs Better
related.hook: Training corpora are full of copies — one 61-word sentence shows up 60,000+ times in C4. Strip the duplicates and models memorize far less and evaluate more honestly.

flashcards.prompt: How does LAION-BVD get captions for 80 million videos?
flashcards.back_html: Content-aware scene detection cuts each video into clips, and video and audio captions for those clips are generated synthetically rather than collected from humans.

flashcards.prompt: Why are scene-changing video frames interesting as image-text training data?

choices.text: Their visual distribution differs from standard web image corpora
They are higher resolution than web images
They come with human-written alt text
They require no licensing because they are frames

flashcards.explanation_html: The authors extract scene-changing frames as an alternative image-text source and note the distribution shift; models trained on them still reach strong image-text retrieval.
